findings.title: DISTINCT with GROUP BY
findings.message: GROUP BY already returns one row per group.
findings.suggestion: Remove DISTINCT unless the select list adds columns outside the groups.
findings.suggestedSql: SELECT o.status, COUNT(*) FROM sales.orders o WHERE o.status = 'NEW' GROUP BY o.status

findings.title: UNION removes duplicates
findings.message: UNION sorts or hashes the result to remove duplicates.
findings.suggestion: Use UNION ALL when the branches cannot overlap or duplicates are fine.
findings.suggestedSql:
SELECT id FROM sales.orders WHERE status = 'A'
UNION ALL
SELECT id FROM sales.orders WHERE status = 'B'
findings.suggestedSqlNote: Changes behavior in edge cases: Only if the branches cannot return the same row and no branch returns duplicates, or if duplicate rows are acceptable: UNION ALL keeps the duplicates UNION removed.

findings.title: Table read several times
findings.message: sales.orders is read 2 times in this statement.
findings.suggestion: Read it once in a CTE (or with conditional aggregation) and reuse the result.

findings.title: Row-by-row DML in a loop
findings.message: This delete runs once per loop iteration.
findings.suggestion: Replace the loop with one set-based statement (INSERT … SELECT, UPDATE … FROM, MERGE), or batch it (FORALL / bulk binds).

findings.title: Correlated subquery in the select list
findings.message: This subquery refers to c.id of the outer query, so it runs once for every row the outer query returns (some optimizers rewrite it, many do not).
findings.suggestion: Compute it once for all rows: join a grouped derived table (LEFT JOIN (SELECT key, agg(…) … GROUP BY key) d ON d.key = outer key) or use a LATERAL join / OUTER APPLY (12c+). Amber offers a verified rewrite for the simple aggregate form.
findings.suggestedSql:
SELECT c.name,
       SQ1.AGG_VALUE AS total
  FROM sales.customers c LEFT JOIN (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.amount) AS AGG_VALUE FROM sales.orders o GROUP BY o.customer_id) SQ1 ON SQ1.customer_id = c.id
findings.suggestedSqlNote: Equivalent given the known metadata. The correlated columns have the same type on both sides (CUSTOMER_ID) in the known metadata, so grouping by the inner column matches each outer row at most once. The structural check sees the new GROUP BY and source.

findings.title: Calculation on a compared column
findings.message: Arithmetic on o.amount (o.amount + 1) is computed for every row before the comparison, so an index on o.amount cannot be used.
findings.suggestion: Move the calculation to the other side of the comparison so the bare column is compared. For example: o.amount = 5 - 1.
findings.suggestedSql: SELECT * FROM sales.orders o WHERE o.amount = 5 - 1
findings.suggestedSqlNote: Same rows for exact numbers and dates; check rounding for floating-point columns.

findings.title: Statements that can be combined
findings.message: This UPDATE changes the same rows of SALES . ORDERS as the UPDATE on line 16 (same WHERE); each UPDATE finds, locks and writes the rows again.
findings.suggestion:
Combine them into one UPDATE (the second does not read what the first sets, so the result is the same; check triggers that count statements):
UPDATE sales.orders SET status = 'X', amount = 0 WHERE customer_id = 7
findings.suggestedSql: UPDATE sales.orders SET status = 'X', amount = 0 WHERE customer_id = 7
findings.suggestedSqlNote: Replaces both UPDATEs. Same result because the second one neither sets nor reads a column the first one sets; row triggers fire once instead of twice.

findings.title: Cursor loop that can be one statement
findings.message: This loop runs one delete per row of its cursor, and the loop body uses nothing but the cursor row; one set-based statement does the same work in a single pass.
findings.suggestion: Replace the loop with one set-based statement (UPDATE … FROM / MERGE, INSERT … SELECT, DELETE … WHERE EXISTS). Check first that the cursor cannot return the same target row twice (aggregate it then), and that no per-row error handling or commit is needed.

statements.original:
SELECT c.name,
       (SELECT SUM(o.amount) FROM sales.orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS total
  FROM sales.customers c
statements.optimized:
SELECT c.name,
       SQ1.AGG_VALUE AS total
  FROM sales.customers c LEFT JOIN (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.amount) AS AGG_VALUE FROM sales.orders o GROUP BY o.customer_id) SQ1 ON SQ1.customer_id = c.id

statements.original: SELECT DISTINCT o.status, COUNT(*) FROM sales.orders o WHERE o.status = 'NEW' GROUP BY o.status
statements.optimized: SELECT o.status, COUNT(*) FROM sales.orders o WHERE o.status = 'NEW' GROUP BY o.status

rules.title: Cartesian product
rules.description: Several tables in FROM without any join or WHERE condition: every row is combined with every row.

rules.title: LEFT JOIN behaves as INNER JOIN
rules.description: A WHERE condition on the right table of a LEFT JOIN drops the rows the outer join kept.

rules.title: Leading wildcard
rules.description: LIKE '%x' cannot use an index on the column.

rules.title: NOT IN with a subquery
rules.description: One NULL from the subquery makes NOT IN match no rows (certain when metadata says the column is nullable).

rules.title: Table read several times
rules.description: The same table is read several times in one statement.

rules.title: Row-by-row DML in a loop
rules.description: An INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE runs once per loop iteration.

rules.title: COMMIT inside a loop
rules.description: Committing every iteration is slow and leaves partial results when the loop fails.

rules.title: Function on a filtered column
rules.description: A function or calculation on a column in WHERE prevents an index on it from being used (HIGH when metadata shows the index).

rules.title: UNION removes duplicates
rules.description: UNION sorts or hashes the result; UNION ALL may be enough.

rules.title: SELECT * written into a table or view
rules.description: The column list changes whenever the source table changes.

rules.title: DISTINCT with GROUP BY
rules.description: GROUP BY already returns one row per group.

rules.title: ORDER BY in a subquery
rules.description: The order of a subquery or CTE without a row limit is not kept by the outer query.

rules.title: Many-to-many join
rules.description: The join columns are unique on neither side, so rows repeat on both sides.

rules.title: Duplicate statement
rules.description: The same statement appears again (literals ignored).

rules.title: Repeated subquery
rules.description: The same subquery appears several times in the script.

rules.title: Dynamic SQL
rules.description: SQL built at run time is not analyzed.

rules.title: Columns without a table
rules.description: Columns that could not be attributed to a table.

rules.title: Possible missing index
rules.description: A column used in joins or filters has no index that starts with it in the known table definition (raised to LOW when used in 3 or more statements). A hint only: check real data volumes and existing indexes.

rules.title: Implicit conversion
rules.description: A column of a known type is compared with a value of another type, so the database converts one side: the column (an index cannot be used) or the value (with session-dependent formats or run-time errors).

rules.title: Correlated subquery in the select list
rules.description: A scalar subquery that refers to the outer row runs once per row; a join to a grouped derived table runs once.

rules.title: Statements that can be combined
rules.description: Consecutive UPDATEs of the same rows, or an UPDATE plus INSERT … WHERE NOT EXISTS on the same table (an upsert), can be one statement.

rules.title: Cursor loop that can be one statement
rules.description: A cursor loop whose body is a single DML using only the cursor row can be written as one set-based statement.

rules.title: OR across indexed columns
rules.description: OR between conditions on different indexed columns of one table can keep any single index from being used.

rules.title: Calculation on a compared column
rules.description: Arithmetic or concatenation on a column in WHERE / ON, or NVL / COALESCE / ISNULL on a join column, keeps an index on it from being used.

rules.title: COUNT used to test existence
rules.description: COUNT(*) > 0 counts every matching row; EXISTS stops at the first one.

rules.title: DISTINCT hiding a duplicating join
rules.description: The selected columns already include a unique key of one table; DISTINCT only removes duplicates the joins produce.
